evidence.exactSufficientQuote: If the enemy successfully invades Muslim territory, then the collective duty transforms into an individual duty. Kâsânî notes that if the level of fear of enemy conquest becomes widespread, because, if for example the enemy has attacked Muslim lands then the duty of jihad transforms into “an individual obligation upon every single physically capable Muslim.”38 He adds: The obligation of jihad rests on all even before there is widespread fear, because it only drops from the rest of the community when some Muslims successfully perform it. When there is widespread fear of conquest, a successful performance can only take place through everyone’s agency. For this reason it remains as an individual duty on everyone, on the same level as the obligation to fast and pray five times a day.39
